## 4. A complete compiler for near-maximal capacity versus zero

The fixed pair already rules out a profile-invariant \(1/4\)-bit capacity evaluator: a common estimate cannot be within \(1/4\) of two capacities separated by at least \(117/128>1/2\).

The stronger construction reaches
\[
\boxed{
Q(\Psi_{k,\epsilon})\ge k-\epsilon,
\qquad
Q(\Phi_{k,\epsilon})=0
}
\]
for every integer \(k\ge1\) and positive rational \(\epsilon\).

The physical cost is explicit.

### A rational encoder and a known error recursion

I instantiated the standard five-qubit code with stabilizers
\[
XZZXI,\quad IXZZX,\quad XIXZZ,\quad ZXIXZ.
\]
Its encoder entries are \(0,\pm1/4\); its recovery operators are explicitly rational. The supplied checks verify all 16 correctable subspaces and classify all 1024 physical Pauli errors exactly. The code itself is established machinery; the exact encoder, recovery, and quantitative compiler are included here. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

After correcting the orthogonal physical flags, the base nonidentity Pauli probability is
\[
p_0=\frac3{512}.
\]
For \(r\) concatenation levels,
\[
p_{r+1}\le10p_r^2,
\qquad
p_r\le
\frac1{10}\left(\frac{15}{256}\right)^{2^r}.
\]

Choose \(L\ge2\) and then \(r\) so that
\[
2^{-L}(L+4)\le\frac{\epsilon}{k},
\qquad
p_r\le2^{-L}.
\]
Both searches terminate using rational comparisons. Set
\[
N=k5^r.
\]

The channels are the actual \(N\)-fold base channels precomposed with the same rational encoding isometry:
\[
\Psi_{k,\epsilon}
=
\Psi_0^{\otimes N}\circ\operatorname{Ad}_V,
\qquad
\Phi_{k,\epsilon}
=
\Phi_0^{\otimes N}\circ\operatorname{Ad}_V.
\]

The high channel has the stated coherent-information lower bound after local recovery. The low channel remains antidegradable. Common input precomposition preserves the complete profile identity.

### Every physical use is paid

| Quantity | Exact convention |
|---|---|
| Logical input | \(k\) qubits |
| Base-channel uses in one compiled use | \(N=k5^r\), computed in advance |
| Actual output dimension | \(8^N\) |
| High-channel capacity lower bound per compiled use | \(k-\epsilon\) |
| Low-channel capacity | \(0\) |
| Exhibited rate per base-channel use | \((k-\epsilon)/N\) |

For the executed example \(k=1,\epsilon=1/128\), one concatenation level suffices:
\[
N=5,\qquad \dim B_{\mathrm{out}}=32768,
\]
and the compiler returns
\[
